findings.evidence: Line 69: `fin_cases i <;> simp; ring`. Here `;` applies `ring` to one leftover goal, not to every case.
findings.fix: Use `fin_cases i <;> simp <;> ring`, or give `simp` the needed `neg_add` lemma so the trailing tactic is unnecessary.
findings.issue: `map_add'` in `timeFirstToNative` uses `fin_cases i <;> simp; ring`. The trailing `ring` only runs on the first goal `simp` leaves open, so the proof breaks if `simp` closes that goal or leaves a different number of goals.

findings.evidence: Lines 183-186 and 269-271 of the diff: each `rw [...]` list has more than 12 entries, most of them elementary sign and scalar lemmas that `simp` handles.
findings.fix: Keep the structural rewrites (`map_mul`, `diracClifford_ι`, `diracVector_mul_diracVector`, the `_ι_eq_neg_mul_adjugate` lemma, `hneg`) and finish with `simp [hX, hY, conjTranspose_mul, adjugate_conjTranspose, fromBlocks_neg]`. In `diracVector_mul_add_mul_swap`, close the scalar bookkeeping with `simp`, or with `linear_combination` on `h`.
findings.issue: `diracClifford_ι_mul_ι` closes its goal with a single `rw` chain of about 17 named lemmas (`map_mul`, `smul_mul_smul_comm`, `conjTranspose_mul`, `adjugate_conjTranspose`, `hX`, `hY`, `neg_mul_neg`, `Complex.I_mul_I`, `neg_one_smul`, `fromBlocks_neg`, `neg_zero`, …). `diracVector_mul_add_mul_swap` (line 269) has the same problem: a 13-lemma `rw … at h` chain followed by `neg_eq_iff_eq_neg`. Both break on any Mathlib rename or change in rewrite order.

summary: Two proofs are long, brittle chains of named-lemma rewrites, and one `; ring` only works if `simp` leaves exactly one goal open.
